title: GPU driver regression hunt and TF CI compatibility matrix
summary: Working notes for a focused regression hunt across driver/CUDA/NCCL permutations with Terraform CI gating and a compact compatibility matrix for private deployments.
content:
Context:
This is a working draft intended to capture an engineering-first, reproducible approach to triaging regressions that arise during GPU driver and CUDA/NCCL upgrades in our private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. The goal is to be prescriptive: which permutations to test in CI, what smoke failures look like, and quick diagnostics to reduce MTTR for Dedicated and Private customers.

Objective:
- Produce a minimal compatibility matrix that our TF modules and CI can use as test vectors.
- Define a regression-hunt checklist for SRE/infra to follow when a rollout begins to show token-level latency regressions, OOMs, or NCCL hangs.
- Surface Terraform module notes and common pitfalls observed in the last three upgrade cycles.

Scope and constraints:
- Focused on x86 GPU hosts (NVIDIA Ampere/Neoverse/Turing families we support). ARM/Graviton hosts are out-of-scope for this note.
- Covers Kubernetes node image, NVIDIA driver, CUDA toolkit, and NCCL runtime interactions.
- Assumes cluster orchestration via our TF modules + kustomize overlays.

Compact compatibility matrix (recommended CI matrix vectors)
(keep this text-parsable for automation):
- driver-525.85 | cuda-11.8 | nccl-2.14 | notes: baseline for 2024 workloads; known good for attention kernels up to seq_len 2048
- driver-535.86 | cuda-12.1 | nccl-2.17 | notes: preferred for newer 80GB cards; watch for subtle fp16 conv regressions
- driver-470.161 | cuda-11.4 | nccl-2.9  | notes: older driver kept for legacy clusters; high latency under heavy batching observed in 2025
- driver-535.86 | cuda-11.8 | nccl-2.15 | notes: mixed CUDA-driver combos we test when vendor backports exist
- driver-470.161 | cuda-10.2 | nccl-2.7  | notes: only for vendors who cannot upgrade; limited to small-token workloads

Why these vectors?
- They represent the smallest useful set that covers: recent supported driver (535.x), stable long-lived driver (525.x), and legacy LTS (470.x). CUDA and NCCL versions chosen to reflect common OS package constraints in customer environments.

Terraform module notes (practical gotchas):
- provider "nvidia_driver": do not rely on latest tag in production; pin exact driver rpm/deb URL. CI should validate checksum.
- node_image variable: image build must include CUDA toolchain that matches the driver installed. Mismatch => silent performance regressions (not just crashes).
- kubelet_args: ensure --feature-gates=DevicePlugins is present for older k8s minor versions. Missing flags manifested as device-plugin flapping in 1:1 tests.
- taints and tolerations: our TF modules previously omitted a nodeSelector for low-latency pools; results in noisy neighbour interference. Add explicit label "gpu.workload=llm-inference" to reserved nodes.
- upgrade_order: terraform apply should be: 1) control plane image, 2) node image build + artifact upload, 3) drain/cordon + driver install, 4) uncordon. Reversing steps led to multiple driver/kernel module version mismatches during last rehearsal.
- driver_install_script: add a preflight check that verifies kernel-headers match running kernel (exit non-zero with diagnostic log if mismatch).

CI gating and test cases (practical):
- unit: lint TF, validate module inputs, terraform plan dry-run.
- infra-smoke (parallelizable per vector): spin 1 node pool with pinned node image + driver, deploy a minimal inference runtime pod (cpu/gpu smoke). Smoke criteria: pod startup <= 90s, device-plugin registers GPUs, nvidia-smi lists expected driver.
- perf-smoke: run a 60s synthetic token-generation (single-stream) and assert p50 latency within 20% of baseline for that vector and no increase in 95th percentile >30%.
- mem-smoke: run multi-stream synthetic workload with batch sizes 1/4/16 to exercise KV cache growth; assert no OOMs in a 5m window.
- nccl-hang-check: run a small NCCL allreduce benchmark (docker image included in artifacts) and require completion within 120s. If hung, capture dmesg + /var/log/nvidia-installer.log + nvtop snapshot.
- reconcile: after smoke tests, run k8s e2e scenario: rolling-update of 5 replicas under load, ensure at least 90% successful inference responses.

Regression-hunt checklist (triage playbook):
1) Reproduce locally in staging using the same TF vector (driver/CUDA/NCCL/node-image). If unreproducible, collect cluster-export (kubectl cluster-info dump).
2) Check node-level metrics: GPU mem pressure, GPU utilization, CPU steal, and kernel dmesg for GPU hangs.
3) Capture runtime logs: inference runtime stdout, nv-hostengine logs, nvidia-smi snapshot. Use "rtlog collect --since=10m --target=pod:inference-runtime" helper.
4) If latency regressed without crashes: check CUDA context creation times and kernel launch times using CUPTI traces (short 30s sampling).
5) For NCCL issues: run the NCCL test container against the same set of nodes; enable NCCL_DEBUG=INFO to collect trace and timestamped join/comm events.
6) If driver mismatch suspected: compare /proc/driver/nvidia/version against the package manifest in the node image.
7) If no clear signal: roll forward a canary using smallest subset of traffic to variant with pinned older driver. Monitor p50/p95, token cost, and OOM rate.

Observed failure modes and notes from past incidents:
- Symptom: intermittent 10–30% token latency spikes on batch sizes >=8 after upgrading to driver-535 on some 80GB cards. Root cause: vendor microcode + driver scheduling mismatch under heavy kernel preemption; temporary mitigation was to add "nvidia-smi -pm 1" persistent mode and reduce preemption granularity.
- Symptom: NCCL allreduce hang with cuda-12.1 driver pair after k8s upgrade; root cause: incompatible iommu setting on certain vendor BIOS. Workaround: set iommu=softdomain on kernel cmdline and revalidate.
- Symptom: silent accuracy drift on int8 quantized ops after moving from cuda-11.8->12.1; root cause: cuBLAS algorithm selection changed. Mitigation: pin cublasMathMode or re-evaluate quantization recipe.

Quick diagnostic commands (copyable):
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv
- sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version || sudo modinfo nvidia | head -n 20
- kubectl -n gpu get pods -o wide --selector=app=inference-runtime
- docker run --rm --gpus=all nvcr.io/nvidia/k8s-device-plugin:stable nvidia-smi
- NCCL: docker run --rm --gpus=all nvcr.io/nvidia/nccl-tests:latest "./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 2048 -f 2"

Rollback guidance (fast path):
- If a staged canary fails perf gates: 1) pause rollout, 2) drain canary nodes, 3) revert TF node image to last known-good artifact, 4) redeploy and uncordon.
- Preserve logs from failing nodes with "tar czf /tmp/failure-logs-$(date +%s).tgz /var/log /var/lib/kubelet" and upload to incident bucket.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should our TF modules expose a lightweight "driver_compatibility_profile" that bundles the triple (driver, cuda, nccl) and auto-selects compatible package sources? (pros: easier for customers; cons: hides compatibility decisions).
- Can we instrument CI to automatically compare kernel launch times across vectors and flag >15% regression? Implementation story: add CUPTI microtrace stage in perf-smoke.
- Add a recurring quarterly matrix validation job that cycles through a prioritized subset of vectors during low-traffic windows.

Appendix: proposed CI test labels for automation (use these labels as job names)
- ci-gpu-smoke.driver-525-cuda-11.8-nccl-2.14
- ci-gpu-smoke.driver-535-cuda-12.1-nccl-2.17
- ci-gpu-smoke.driver-470-cuda-11.4-nccl-2.9

Notes to self:
- When we add ARM hosts, expand matrix but keep the same triage checklist.
- Share this doc with solutions-eng before finalizing the driver compatibility bundle proposal.

-- end of draft --
